label: Early original-phase input (steps 2-4) of l/i/g/0/d/b/o/w
explanation: Reset-gate unit that fires almost only on early steps of the original phase: t=2 (49% of activation mass), t=3 (41%), and t=4 (10%). It never fires at t=0, almost never at t=1 or t>=5, and essentially never in the copy phase. About 6% of the mass is on the <DEL> step, mostly in short sequences (L=3-4). Within the t=2-4 window, the input token sets the rate: l, i and g fire most (about 19% of all their steps), then 0, d, b, o and w, then q, m and a; other letters rarely fire. It fires mainly on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=1 holds 94% of the mass). The largest activations are l, i or g at t=3, often in sequences that start with j or e; prefix tokens like these raise the rate about 2x, which the predicate does not capture. A predicate for steps 2-3 with the 8-token set plus step 4 with l/i/g gets dev F1 of about 0.71 and mass recall of about 0.81. The misses are lower-ranked tokens and <DEL> steps; the false positives are favored tokens in prefixes that do not push the unit over threshold.
